Article 17

Letter a

Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b

Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c

Sexual violence is caused by:

1) acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2) coercion of sexual intercourse;
3) coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4) coercion of sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Letter d

Neglect is caused by:

1) acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of a Child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2) acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as they should, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3) acts of abandoning a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by reason of agreement or covenant they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4) acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e

Mistreatment is mistreatment of the physical and emotional state of a Child including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from incorrect human behavior toward the Child.

Letter f

Exploitation is caused by:

1) acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced work or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3) all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g

Other violence is caused by:

1) threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of words, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2) coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

4) acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e

Mistreatment is mistreatment of the physical and emotional state of a Child including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from incorrect human behavior toward the Child.

Letter f

Exploitation is caused by:

1) acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced work or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3) all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g

Other violence is caused by:

1) threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of words, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2) coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter d

Letter e

The principle of openness reflects the implementation of protection for victims of violence in a transparent manner.

Letter f

The principle of protection provides protection to victims of acts of violence, guarantees the confidentiality, security, safety of life and psychological well-being of victims.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, given their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government

of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children who are victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and Children from acts of Violence is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of the Society, especially to women and Children, among others, due to the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling is not yet well coordinated, its implementation is not yet sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to address and at the same time provide legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children who are victims of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support from both the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is expected that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Article 1

1. Region is Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Hulu Sungai Selatan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government organizer.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not been married including a Child who is still in the womb.
15. Victim of Acts of Violence is a woman and Child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the Community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and Children.
17. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency Government in providing services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.

19. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing the Community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and Community environment that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
20. Recovery of Victims hereinafter Recovery is a service provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and Children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
21. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and Children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
22. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
23. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

2) coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children who are victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and Children from acts of Violence is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of the Society, especially to women and Children, among others, due to the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling is not yet well coordinated, its implementation is not yet sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to address and at the same time provide legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children who are victims of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support from both the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is expected that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Hulu Sungai Selatan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government organizer.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not been married including a Child who is still in the womb.
15. Victim of Acts of Violence is a woman and Child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the Community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and Children.
17. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency Government in providing services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.
18. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
19. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing the Community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and Community environment that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
20. Recovery of Victims hereinafter Recovery is a service provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and Children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
21. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and Children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
22. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
23. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), in accordance with the regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 24

a. notification of job opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(4) Partnership as referred to in paragraph (3) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, given their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government

of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children who are victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and Children from acts of Violence is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of the Society, especially to women and Children, among others, due to the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling is not yet well coordinated, its implementation is not yet sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to address and at the same time provide legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children who are victims of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support from both the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is expected that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, given their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government

of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children who are victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and Children from acts of Violence is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of the Society, especially to women and Children, among others, due to the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling is not yet well coordinated, its implementation is not yet sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to address and at the same time provide legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children who are victims of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support from both the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is expected that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Hulu Sungai Selatan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of the Regional Government organizer.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not been married including a Child who is still in the womb.
15. Victim of Acts of Violence is a woman and Child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the Community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and Children.
17. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency Government in providing services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.
18. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
19. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing the Community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and Community environment that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
20. Recovery of Victims hereinafter Recovery is a service provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and Children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
21. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and Children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
22. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
23. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 30

Funding for the implementation of protection of women and children from violence as regulated in this Regional Regulation is charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other legitimate and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 31

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that carry out the protection of women and children from discrimination and violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), in accordance with the regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government grants awards to every person or entity that participates in efforts to protect women and children from violence in the Region.

(2) Awards as referred to in paragraph (1) are given in the form of: a. certificates/plaques; and

b. regional incentives.

(3) Incentives as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b can be in the form of: a. fiscal; and

b. non-fiscal.

(4) Fiscal incentives as referred to in paragraph (3) letter a can be in the form of: a. reduction or exemption of regional taxes; and/or

b. reduction of regional levies.

(5) Non-fiscal incentives as referred to in paragraph (3) letter b can be in the form of ease of regional licensing in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(6) The procedures and forms of granting incentives as referred to in paragraph (2) are guided by the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 34

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of its promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, given their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government

of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children who are victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and Children from acts of Violence is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of a Regional Regulation as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of the Society, especially to women and Children, among others, due to the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling is not yet well coordinated, its implementation is not yet sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to address and at the same time provide legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children who are victims of acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support from both the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is expected that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Hulu Sungai Selatan.

5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not been married including a Child who is still in the womb.
15. Victim of Acts of Violence is a woman and Child who experiences suffering physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the Community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and Children.
17. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency Government in providing services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.
18. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
19. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing the Community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and Community environment that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims.
20. Recovery of Victims hereinafter Recovery is a service provided in the form of strengthening and developing the capabilities of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and Children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
21. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and Children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
22. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
23. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 21

Article 17

Letter a

Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b

Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c

Sexual violence is caused by:

1) acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2) coercion of sexual intercourse;
3) coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4) coercion of sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Letter d

Neglect is caused by:

1) acts that result in the unfulfillment of the needs of a Child properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2) acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as they should, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3) acts of abandoning a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or by reason of agreement or covenant they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4) acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e

Mistreatment is mistreatment of the physical and emotional state of a Child including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from incorrect human behavior toward the Child.

Letter f

Exploitation is caused by:

1) acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced work or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3) all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letter g

Other violence is caused by:

1) threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of words, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2) coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.
